clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau didn't write his first book until after he'd generated about $18 billion in sales.

His pointed question for the personal-development world: Tony Robbins, Bob Proctor, Joe Vitale, Brian Tracy - great teachers, but they made their money selling courses on how to succeed, not from building a business first.

His challenge to them: if you know so much, how come you don't just build one and make a billion dollars first?

So that's what he did - a marketing empire, TV networks, mining operations - before he ever wrote a word of advice.

Would you trust advice more from someone who built it, or someone who just teaches it?

clips.end_words: you either win or you learn
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau watched Jeff Bezos launch an online bookstore before almost anyone saw the internet as real money. "This guy is a winner," Kevin thought - and he was right.

Years later, someone brought him a different opportunity: buy Bitcoin at $20. He said no - fake money, made no sense to him. It came back around at $20,000. Still said no. He missed it completely.

Here's how he keeps that from wrecking him: you never actually get it wrong. You either win, or you learn. Most people are so afraid of a bad decision that they never make one.

What opportunity are you still punishing yourself for missing?

#kevintrudeau #mindset #wealthmindset #investing #entrepreneur #successhabits

Kevin Trudeau says it's easier to make money today than at any point in history - so anybody who can't is either a fool or an expert at making excuses.

Back in the old days you needed inventory, a storefront, real capital. That's why multi-level marketing - Amway, Mary Kay, Herbalife - got so big: it was the only way in for someone without money or connections.

Today you don't need any of that. No special knowledge, no capital required, and people are building fortunes doing it.

A failure is always good at one thing: making excuses.

What's the excuse you've been hiding behind?
